references.text: The description of the holy garments to be made for Aaron to give him dignity and splendor in his priestly service.
Instructions on how to clothe Aaron in the holy garments and anoint him as part of the consecration ceremony.
The command to anoint Aaron and his sons to set them apart for priestly service before the Lord.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses clothes Aaron in the holy garments and anoints him to set him apart.
Reference to Aaron's sons who were anointed and consecrated for priestly service.
A poetic description of the anointing oil that ran down over Aaron's head and beard, a reference to the priestly anointing.
Explanation of the high priest's role as one appointed on behalf of people, and that no one takes this honor upon themselves unless called by God, just as Aaron was.
Comparison between the Levitical priesthood and Christ's priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek.
Describes the same consecration ritual and expands the instruction from Aaron to also include his sons.
Highlights the connection between the sanctification of the priest and the sanctification of the sanctuary (the tent and the altar).
Complements the source verse by specifying which garments are included in the consecration ritual.
